## 2026-11-25 — v0.67.4

### Changed

- **foxguard pin 0.14.1 -> 0.14.2.** `CI_DEFAULT_FOXGUARD_VERSION` and its five SHA-256 values in `lib/ci_defaults.sh`, copied from the release's `checksums.txt`; the asset digests and a local download agree. `ci_security.sh` now treats a foxguard older than 0.14.2 on `PATH` as out of date. The test stubs that stand for the pinned version report 0.14.2.

### Fixed

- **The foxguard push gate refuses a push when one of its working files cannot be written.** `sec_foxguard_scan` built the list of skipped files with `{ grep | grep -v > <out>.skipped; } || true`: a failed write left the list empty, and a pushed file foxguard could not parse passed as "nothing skipped". The other lists had the same gap. An empty map of the pushed files scanned nothing, so a new finding passed with no message; a changed file that could not be added to the file list was never scanned; a base lost from the base list was not scanned and not counted as missing. Each of these writes is now checked, and so are the sort of the file list, the real name of a file scanned from its own directory, the `noise path` skip line and the base config. A failure refuses the push and says `Check that <directory> is writable and has free space`, not to install foxguard. A write that fails while a file is scanned (the skip list, the real name, the `noise path` line) refuses as `the foxguard scan failed`, which names both remedies: install the pinned foxguard, and check that the directory is writable and has free space. The skip list is written by the shell, one checked write per file. A rerun of a file from its own directory that writes no report is no longer read as the empty report of the first run. A write that fails without an error is caught too: the base list, the base file maps and the map of the pushed files are counted after the write, and each copy of a file to scan is read back and compared (`sec_foxguard_tree` trusted `sed` to report a failed write). The copy of the base config and the read of a pushed config are checked: under `set -e` a failure there ended the hook with no message. Tests: `tests/foxguard_block_test.sh` (fail without the fix).
- **The foxguard push gate refuses two pushed paths that are one file where it writes its copies.** On a case-insensitive file system (the default on macOS and Windows) `App.py` and `app.py` are one file: the second copy replaced the first in the scanned tree, so the first was never scanned and a new finding in it passed. `sec_foxguard_tree` returns 2 when the name it is about to write is already there, and the push is refused with the name and `Rename one of them, or point TMPDIR at a case-sensitive file system`. On a case-sensitive file system both files are scanned as before. A file where a directory of the next path must be (`A` and `a/x.py`) is the same clash and gets the same refusal; it used to say `the pushed files could not be read` and to check that the directory is writable. Tests: `tests/foxguard_block_test.sh` (fail without the fix).
- **The foxguard push gate scans a file whose extension is not in lower case.** foxguard reads `app.py` and leaves `app.PY` or `x.Js` out as an unsupported extension, which the gate does not count as a skip: a new finding in such a file passed the push with no message, and the file runs all the same (`python app.PY`). `sec_foxguard_scan` now scans it as a copy named with the extension in lower case and reports it under its own name; one it cannot parse is a skip like any other. `.C` and `.H` are scanned as C, so `system(argv[1])` in `Util.C` blocks. One that does not parse as C is C++, which foxguard does not read: it is printed as `not scanned` and counted, and does not refuse the push (a push refused for another file it could not read names it too); as a base copy it is unscanned, so a finding in the new file blocks as `the base copy could not be scanned`. Tests: `tests/foxguard_block_test.sh` (fail without the fix).
- **The foxguard push gate scans a file foxguard tells by its path, in a noise path.** foxguard reads an nginx or Apache config for its path (`nginx/`, `conf.d/`), and drops `nginx/build/site.conf` as noise. The gate scanned such a file again from its own directory, where `site.conf` is an unsupported extension: a new finding in it passed the push with no message. A file in a noise path is now scanned as a copy that keeps its directories, each with `d_` in front (`d_nginx/d_build/site.conf`), never from its own directory: there `nginx/build/apache.conf` was read as an Apache config, and an nginx finding in it passed. The copies made for a noise name and an upper-case extension keep the directories too. The prefix is `d_`, not `_`: `_tests__` became the noise path `__tests__`, and a new finding in `src/_tests__/Loader.PY` passed with no message. Tests: `tests/foxguard_block_test.sh` (fail without the fix).
- **The foxguard push gate scans a file foxguard tells by its name, with a noise name.** foxguard reads `nginx.conf`, `my-nginx.conf`, `Dockerfile.dev` and `haproxy.cfg` for their name, and drops `nginx.min.conf` as noise. The gate scanned such a file as a copy named `<n>.conf`, an unsupported extension, which it does not count as a skip: a new finding in it passed the push with no message, at `off` too. A copy now keeps its name but for the noise part (`nginx._min.conf`, `app._min.js`), and one made for an upper-case extension keeps it too (`Cargo.LOCK` as `Cargo.lock`); `<n>.<extension>` is the name of last resort. foxguard calls only a file type it knows noise, so a file that no copy got read is listed as skipped (`noise path`) and refuses the push, whatever the last copy was left out for. A test pushes every name foxguard 0.14.2 reads (50 extensions, the files told by their name and by their path) as it is, in a noise path, with a noise name and with an upper-case extension, 466 files, and checks that foxguard read each one, at `high` and at `off`. Tests: `tests/foxguard_block_test.sh` (fail without the fix).
- **At `security.foxguardBlock off` the foxguard warning leaves no changed file out without a word.** `sec_foxguard_warn` gave each file to foxguard as it is: one in a noise path (`a/build/x.py`), with a noise name (`app.min.js`) or with an upper-case extension (`app.PY`) was not read, and one foxguard could not parse printed nothing. Each is now printed as `not scanned: <path> (<reason>)` and counted in a warning: `noise path`, `upper-case extension`, `parse error`, or foxguard's own reason (over 1 MB). No copy is scanned at `off`: every file is scanned where it is, under the foxguard config of the working tree, so a rule the config turns off (`disable_rules`) is not reported for any file; a blocking level scans those files. Whether foxguard reads an extension in lower case is asked of an empty file of that name under `TMPDIR` (nothing of the file is copied), so `NOTES.TXT` and `logo.PNG` are not named. A name that starts with a dash is given as `./-x.py`, not read as an option. Why a file was left out is read from foxguard's summary line (`Skipped 1 file: 1 parse error.`), not from a line that carries a file name or a line of code: a file named `Skipped 1 file: 1 unsupported extension..py` that does not parse is named as `not scanned`, and one with a finding on a line that holds `Skipped 1 file: 1 noise path.` is not. The push goes on as before. Tests: `tests/foxguard_block_test.sh` (fail without the fix).
- **The foxguard push gate says why it refuses a path that is not valid UTF-8.** foxguard takes no such argument, so the scan failed and the refusal advised installing foxguard. The names are now checked first (`foxguard_push_compare.py --names <list>`, exit 4): the refusal prints the path with its odd bytes as `\xNN` and says to rename it. A push that renames such a file is not refused: the old name is never given to foxguard. Tests: `tests/foxguard_block_test.sh` and `tests/foxguard_push_compare_test.sh` (both fail without the fix).
- **The foxguard push gate does not send a control character in a file name to the terminal.** A carriage return or an escape sequence in the name of a skipped or flagged file was printed as it is, and drew the name over the `[pre-push] BLOCK` or `WARNING` in front of it. A skip line now shows it as `?`, and a finding as `\xNN` (`a\x0db.py`). The same is done for the C1 controls (U+009B starts an escape sequence on some terminals) and the characters that reorder, hide or break text (U+202E, U+200E, U+200F, U+200B, U+2028, U+2029, U+FEFF and the like): `?` in a skip line, `\x9b` or `\u202e` in a finding. Both sides hide the same ones: a test gives every code point from U+0080 to U+2FFFF to both. The comparison still uses the real name. `foxguard_push_compare.py` prints its lines as UTF-8 whatever the locale: under a Windows Python a file name outside cp1252 failed the print, and the push was refused with `the foxguard reports could not be compared`; its lines end in a line feed there too, not in a carriage return and a line feed. A finding with no rule prints `-` for it, so the hook does not read the reason as the rule. At `off` the lines of foxguard's own report, which carry the file name as it is, and the first lines of a failed scan are shown the same way (`a?b.py`); its progress, which starts with a carriage return, is left out, and a message of its own that follows it on the same line (`Warning: unknown rule id in config`) is still shown. Tests: `tests/foxguard_block_test.sh` and `tests/foxguard_push_compare_test.sh` (both fail without the fix).
- **The foxguard push gate scans a file whose name is pathspec magic.** `sec_foxguard_tree` asked git for each file with `git ls-tree -- <path>`, which reads a name such as `:(top)x.py` or `:!x.py` as pathspec magic, found nothing, and left the file out: it was never scanned, and a new finding in it passed the push with no message. The path is now literal (`git --literal-pathspecs`), and a failing `git ls-tree` refuses the push instead of dropping the file. A changed file under a directory whose name starts with a dash (`-z/app.py`) refused every push with `the pushed files could not be read`, because `dirname` took the path for an option; it is scanned like any other file. Test: `tests/foxguard_block_test.sh` (fails without the fix).
- **The foxguard push gate says why a file whose remote copy it could not scan blocks, and takes an opt-in override.** When the copy on the remote was skipped (a parse error, or over 1 MB), it had no findings to compare with, so every finding in the newly readable file counted as new and the push was refused as `(new)`, with no way through short of turning foxguard off. Those findings still block by default, now as `the base copy could not be scanned (<reason>)`, with the base skip printed and a hint to review the file. `SCRIPT_HELPERS_FOXGUARD_ALLOW_UNSCANNED_BASE=1` on that push turns them into warnings that name the override. It covers only files whose base copy was skipped, and with several bases only files that every base having them skipped (a base without the file does not count against it; a file no base has is new); a new finding in any other file still blocks, and once the readable copy lands the file is compared as usual. `foxguard_push_compare.py` takes `--base-unscanned <list>` and `--base-absent <list>` (the files that base does not have) after the `--base` they belong to and `--allow-unscanned`, and exits 2 on a list it cannot read or one with no `--base` before it, with or without the override. When a base is not scanned at all (its scan failed, its files could not be read or listed, or it is past the 8 bases the gate reads), no file counts as skipped by every base: the hook passes `--base-incomplete`, the finding blocks with `another base was not scanned, so SCRIPT_HELPERS_FOXGUARD_ALLOW_UNSCANNED_BASE=1 does not apply`, and the refusal does not advise the override. A skipped file is listed under its real path: one scanned from its own directory (`src/dist/app.py`) used to be listed as `app.py`, which named the `app.py` at the root instead. A carriage return in a file name no longer splits a skip line in two, and outside Windows `a\b.py` and `a/b.py` are two files, in the skip list and in the comparison; Python under MSYS or Cygwin counts as Windows. The real name of a file scanned from its own directory keeps a carriage return too, so `vendor/x.py<CR>` is not read as a skipped `vendor/x.py`. A parse error in a file with `noise path` in its name is listed once, not also as a noise path. Tests: `tests/foxguard_block_test.sh` and `tests/foxguard_push_compare_test.sh` (both fail without the fix).
- **`setup_traps` prints the exit code of a failed script.** The EXIT handler read `$?` after its own `[[ ]]` guard, so `cleanup` always saw 0 and "Script failed with exit code N" never printed. The handler now passes `$?` to `cleanup` before the guard runs; the script still exits with its own status, also when `trap_stack` chains onto the trap. On INT and TERM the handler now also prints "Script failed with exit code 130" (or 143) after "Script interrupted" (or "Script terminated"). `ci_pimcore_bundle_check.sh` and `ci_wp_plugin_check.sh` had the same pattern in their `cleanup_stack` traps; there the status only fed `return`, which bash ignores in an EXIT trap, so their exit status was never wrong. Covered by `tests/traps_test.sh` (exit 0, 1, 3, `set -e`, a failing subshell, INT, TERM; fails without the fix).
